items.title: Steve "Ted" Brown Interview, 1958-04-22
items.q: Oh, yes. A great many times he'd have bands, he'd dance us downtown, and he'd give us a job.

ctx.x: He deserved credit. Well, he was, in reality, a pioneer in the jazz field. And there was other colored bands that were up there. This was before Louis Armstrong came up there. This was before King Oliver and all those came up. King Oliver and the bands that King Oliver played, and Armstrong, when they first come up to New Orleans, it wasn't a Dick's land combination at all. They had violins, they had flutes, and they had about eight, ten, twelve men, so you understand. And they played regular music at all the…
Yeah, Oliver, I think, got there about 1918, she saw it. And you say Papa Lane had mostly just the brass band. Mostly the brass band. And didn't do much dance work. No.

He'd take it to the small band. But I mean, you could see what... He'd play drums if he, maybe in the small combination. But I mean, I don't remember seeing, we didn't have no competition with these bands at all. In fact, the only bands that gave us competition, in respect, was Fisher's Band. And that band there, in the estimation of the dancers, and the people that I talked to that employed us, were second-raders in comparison to our band.
